venture.description: Rechargeable, app-controlled wall sconces that install with adhesive tape instead of hardwiring.
venture.note: The product includes a physical light and a companion app.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 and F2 deliver their prepared presentation, demonstrating the wall light and its app features.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 expresses approval of the product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if the adhesive damages the wall when removed.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 answers that the adhesive does not damage the wall when removed.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks where the power button is located on the device.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains that the power button is at the bottom of the light.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 handles the prototype and finds the power button.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 handles the prototype and examines its construction.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 compliments the product idea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 notes that the product shown is a prototype from their first round of tooling.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 jokingly warns against dropping the prototype.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 compliments the quality of the tooling.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for the retail price of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the retail price is ninety-five dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for the manufacturing cost.

turns.speaker: F1

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if they will sell direct-to-consumer and suggests the price is high.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that testing showed customers responded better to a higher price with a larger discount.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 disagrees that the price is too high.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for clarification on the discount strategy.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how long the battery charge lasts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides the charging time and the battery life duration.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if there are competing stick-on wall lights in the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that they could not find any and have secured patents.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what aspects the patents cover.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 details their design patent and pending utility patents for the swivel and attachment mechanisms.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks about their sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shares their successful Kickstarter campaign revenue and the speed at which they met their goal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses amazement at the sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 adds that they are facing inventory issues and will run out soon.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if the revenue was solely to fulfill Kickstarter orders.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if they have shipped any units yet.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 confirms they have not shipped yet.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks about orders outside of the crowdfunding campaign.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 mentions their website and credits F2's social media skills.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 reacts playfully to F2 being a social media expert.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 also reacts playfully to F2's social media status.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains they went viral on TikTok, driving organic sales.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for the specific online sales figures post-Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have made about five thousand dollars since the website launched.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if the founders still hold full-time jobs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms they both work full-time to help fund the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what their full-time professions are.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 describes her background in tech and data, and shares her grandfather's immigration story.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 congratulates F2 on her grandfather's story.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains she is a licensed clinical social worker who enjoys figuring out how things work.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 offers a deal with an equity stake and a royalty that drops after a threshold.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 expresses surprise that S1 included a royalty in his offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 remarks that S1's offer is actually quite good.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 agrees his offer is good and praises the founders.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokingly takes credit for S1's generous offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 offers a deal with no equity but a high perpetual royalty per unit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 clarifies the terms of S3's offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 reacts with shock to S3's royalty demand.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 jokingly asks if S3 makes enough money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 playfully replies that she does not make enough money.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks when S3's royalty ends.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 confirms the royalty never ends.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 repeats that the royalty is never-ending.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 jokes that S3 and S1 have swapped personalities.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 advises the founders against taking S3's offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 praises the founders but exits, advising them to take S1's offer over S3's.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks S4 what she plans to do.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 exits, citing concerns about competition in the stick-on lighting market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends their product against S4's concerns, highlighting their hidden tape design.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, expressing doubt that the product is truly damage-free and transient.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attempts to clarify a point.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 urges the founders to focus on the remaining offers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks S3 if she would consider lowering her royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters S3 with a lower perpetual royalty.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 revises her offer to include a line of credit alongside cash for the lower royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 notes that S3's revised offer is very good.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 presses the founders to make a decision.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 counters S1, asking to lower the repayment threshold for his royalty.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 refuses the counter, maintaining his original terms.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts S1's original offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses shock that they chose S1's offer over hers.
